title: fix(macos): unblock updates with protected Bun service commands
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app rejects its own managed `bun --no-install … gateway` command, leaving update and recovery verification incomplete even when the Gateway is healthy.

Fixes #169662.

## User Impact

Valid protected Bun services can reach the app's existing ownership and recovery verification. No configuration or service argument changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`GatewayLaunchAgentManager.installedServiceCLI` skipped memory flags but treated `--no-install` as a second entrypoint. Recognize that exact flag only for a Bun executable, while retaining the full command prefix and all existing entrypoint, wrapper, custody, and runtime-pin checks.

## Evidence

- Compiled native regression: the same two `GatewayServiceRuntimeTests` fail before the fix (four assertions; protected commands return `nil`) and pass after it. After: 2 tests passed in 0.018 seconds; 2.17 seconds including runner startup.
- Coverage includes the packaged Bun command, mixed memory/protective flags, complete `prefix` and `sourcePrefix`, canonical environment wrappers, and rejection of Node plus `--no-install`, `--no-install=true`, and unknown flags.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --jobs 4` passed: 369.32 seconds cold, 92.51 seconds incremental. The source-only checkout first needed `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs` to generate native resource assets.
- Local native tests used the compiled SwiftPM test helper under the repository's macOS sandbox policy, with process spawning and window-server access also denied, filtered to `GatewayServiceRuntimeTests/.*service CLI`. No live Gateway or interactive app recovery was exercised; the full native suite remains CI coverage.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean at P2, no actionable findings.
- Broader local check is not green: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed formatting, lint, dependency, and schema guards, but the unchanged `test/scripts/mac-elevation-host.test.ts` has timed out in installer recovery cases at 120 seconds. At observation time the shared host load was 127.8 across 32 logical CPUs. These shell-fixture workflows do not execute the changed Swift parser. No timeouts, assertions, retries, or test configuration were weakened. The completed first group recorded 117 passed and five timed out in 839.46 seconds. Those failures remain unresolved and were not rerun or relabeled as passing.


- After launcher shutdown interrupted the second tooling group, the same command was rerun with one worker: `pnpm test:macos:ci:2` passed **498 tests in 12 files**, 322.76 seconds of test time (326.17 seconds including the wrapper).
- The remaining `pnpm test:macos:ci:3` group passed **286 tests in 13 files** across eight shards in 316.40 seconds. No source changes were needed for either result.

<details>
<summary>Original elevation recovery timeout cases</summary>

All five used the existing 120-second limit in `test/scripts/mac-elevation-host.test.ts`:

- `explicitly recovers the prior app and source job from the verified install receipt`: 125.625 seconds.
- `restores a verified backup when the current app is missing`: 120.864 seconds.
- `resumes exact app and migration custody after process death`: 120.200 seconds.
- `resumes after the restored prior owner restarted before process death`: 125.081 seconds.
- `resumes an initially absent app after process death`: 120.294 seconds.

These tests compose full shell installer, receipt, and recovery workflows on isolated fixtures. The host was heavily contended; no baseline replay established a repair for their timeout behavior. The production Swift parser is not exercised by these fixture workflows.

</details>

## Proof

- Fresh focused native proof on `c3810638000b39c65cb3de32b1098bc10c2de5de`: **2 GatewayServiceRuntimeTests passed** (0.172 seconds in Swift Testing; 15.636 seconds wall including runner startup). The filter was `GatewayServiceRuntimeTests/.*service CLI`.
- Built the native test bundle under the shared macOS build lock. The initial build failed before tests because Xcode's platform macro plugins were absent from SwiftPM's search path. Supplying the installed platform plugin directory with `-external-plugin-path` resolved that toolchain issue; the corrected build passed in 798.246 seconds. No source or dependency changes were made.
- The sandboxed `swift test --skip-build` entry point could not prepare its package manifest under the operator-file restrictions. The same compiled SwiftPM bundle and filter passed through the repository's documented `swiftpm-testing-helper` route with operator files, preferences, Keychain services, network, process spawning, and WindowServer access restricted. No live Gateway or interactive recovery was exercised.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean at P1**, one completed reviewer pass, no actionable P0/P1 findings. An earlier preparation attempt stopped before a reviewer ran because the worktree was still being populated; the completed review used the stable, unchanged head.
